key_facts: In Milpitas, California, local authorities ordered the operators of the Newby Island landfill to use drones and install monitors to systematically track and measure odour-causing chemicals, and to automate collection of landfill gases responsible for smells.

In Des Moines, Iowa, city authorities spend around $240,000 a year on a ring of odour monitors combined with a weather station to provide real-time data on concentrations from each facility based on wind patterns; Smithfield Foods says it invested $2m in a regenerative thermal oxidiser but denies being the source of complaints.

The US Environmental Protection Agency does not regulate environmental odours as a pollutant, leaving states and local governments to handle the issue; many countries have no odour regulations. Best industrial odour-control technologies can remove 90% or more of target compounds when used correctly, while cheaper masking with deodorisers is considered ineffective by odour experts.

Experts say that urban sprawl and rising land values bring residential development closer to odorous facilities, increasing demand for monitoring technologies; the article also notes the traditional olfactometry (human panels) is still common.

region: Middle East (Strait of Hormuz, Gulf region)
key_facts: Twelve vessels reported attacks in and around the Strait of Hormuz between 5 and 11 October, the largest weekly number reported to UKMTO since the US-Israeli war with Iran began; the previous week saw 10. Six were struck on Sunday, a one-day high.

Middle East oil flows through the strait were about 12.6 million barrels per day on 13 October, down from 15 million at the end of September and below a pre-war baseline of about 17 million bpd (Kpler data).

US Navy data shows vessels given assisted navigation through the strait in the first 10 days of October rose 85% versus the same period in August. Iran calls the shuttle route near Oman's coast 'unauthorised'.

Attacks extended beyond the strait: the tanker Petro Dolphin was hit by a drone near Sohar Anchorage, Oman, over 250 km away; a tanker was struck north of Qatar on 8 October (more than 500 km away); another was attacked near Al-Jazirah al-Hamra, UAE, on 9 October. Two Indian seafarers from the Petro Dolphin are reported missing.

The container ship GFS Pride sank after a strike by an unknown projectile in the strait on Tuesday; 21 crew were evacuated. Iran's IRGC says the ship carried '2,500 containers of contraband' and took an unauthorised route.
importance_reason: Systemic disruption to Gulf oil export flows with a sustained, quantified drop in throughput and widening attacks beyond the strait, though no direct benchmark price move is cited in the source.
market_link: Reduced Gulf crude throughput (about 12.6 mb/d vs 15 mb/d late September and ~17 mb/d pre-war) and expanding attack zone raise supply-risk premium on crude oil and freight/insurance costs for tankers.

key_facts: The U.S. finished fiscal year 2026 with a budget deficit of $1.992 trillion, about 12% higher than the $1.775 trillion deficit in the prior fiscal year, according to the Treasury Department.
It is the third-highest annual deficit in U.S. history, behind 2020 and 2021; FY2026 marked the 25th straight fiscal year of deficit, with the last surplus recorded in 2001.
Social Security was the largest spending item at nearly $1.7 trillion, Medicare second at almost $1.1 trillion, and net interest topped $1 trillion (vs. $970 billion in FY2025).

Individual income tax receipts exceeded $2.8 trillion (up about 7% y/y); corporate income tax receipts were $381 billion, down about $70 billion due to tax cuts in the One Big Beautiful Bill Act. Customs revenue was hit by refunds after a Supreme Court ruling, even as gross customs duties hit a record high.
importance_reason: Full-year fiscal data showing a near $2 trillion deficit and net interest above $1 trillion is a significant macro signal, amplified by recent 10- and 30-year Treasury yields at 24-year highs.
market_link: Persistent large deficits and rising debt-service costs can pressure long-term Treasury yields, bond demand, and the dollar, while higher issuance needs keep attention on bond-market term premiums.
